title: Cost of renting Nvidia H100 computing power rises 60% in a year
key_facts: The Wall Street Journal reports a shortage of AI computing power is reshaping Silicon Valley: rivals form alliances and executives join negotiations.
SemiAnalysis says the hourly cost of renting Nvidia H100 computing power under a one-year contract is up 60% over the past year.
Cloud providers increasingly require multi-year contracts with upfront payments of up to 30%, sometimes with extra financial guarantees.
Some companies sign for more capacity than they need as protection against shortages; others try to resell unused capacity.
Anthropic agreed in May to lease more than 300 megawatts of capacity from Musk's SpaceX, later reported as worth up to $45 billion.
Alphabet expects capital expenditure of as much as $200 billion this year, mostly for AI infrastructure.
Data centres take years to build, held back by regulation and political opposition.
quote_evidence: According to SemiAnalysis, an AI data and consulting firm, the hourly cost of renting computing power from Nvidia H100 chips under a one-year contract has increased by 60 per cent over the past year.
Cloud providers are increasingly requiring multi-year contracts with upfront payments of up to 30 per cent, sometimes accompanied by additional financial guarantees.
Some companies are signing contracts for more computing capacity than they actually need in order to protect themselves against future shortages.
why_it_matters_hint: AI computing power is scarce, with H100 rental prices up about 60% and stricter contracts.
notes: WSJ report relayed by BGNES; date not stated.
